name: Bottled drinking water (purified, spring, artesian)
anchor: strictest applicable sovereign drinking-water or packaged-water maximum, per litre of finished product as consumed, with natural mineral water kept as the separate product form the instruments themselves treat it as (Hong Kong Cap 132V writes dedicated natural-mineral-water lines; EU Directive 2020/2184 excludes the form from its scope)
cross_reference: Flavoured, sweetened or functional waters route to HMTc Category 5 (Beverages). Natural mineral water is the mineral-water row of this category.
native_basis_label: as consumed, per litre of finished bottled water (µg/L; numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
scope_note: This row is packaged water as placed on the market and assessed per litre as consumed. It is governed by the packaged-water bridge stated in the category method note: national drinking-water maxima apply because the product is the same substance in the same basis, and because FDA incorporates the EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulation MCLs into the bottled-water standard of quality at 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) while the scope of EU Directive 2020/2184 expressly reaches water put into bottles or containers. In scope: purified, distilled, deionised, reverse-osmosis, spring, artesian and well water sold packaged for drinking, unflavoured and unsweetened, in any container. Out of scope: natural mineral water, which is a legally distinct product form with its own row and its own instrument (EU Directive 2009/54/EC and Commission Directive 2003/40/EC; the Hong Kong Cap 132V line for this row reads 'bottled or packaged drinking waters, OTHER THAN natural mineral waters'); unflavoured carbonated water, which has its own row; and any flavoured, sweetened, mineral-fortified, vitamin-added or functional water, which routes to HMTc Category 5 (Beverages) by the Category 8 boundary rule because flavouring changes both the matrix and the regulatory treatment. Water sold for formula preparation routes to the infant nursery-water row.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(dry weight|dry matter|dehydrated|migration|leach|material content|surface|\bfeed\b|fat basis))(?=.*(water|as[ _]?consumed|mg/l|placed on market|food as listed)).*$
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a dietary per-litre / as-consumed water or food-schedule basis. The guard rejects dry-weight, dehydrated, migration/leachate, article material-content and feed bases outright, so a dry-commodity maximum level or a food-contact migration limit can never anchor a per-litre water cell. It admits mg/kg-expressed food-schedule rows (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011) because potable water density is within 0.3 per cent of 1 kg/L, so µg/kg and µg/L are the same number to well inside analytical uncertainty; that is a stated identity, not a silent conversion.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; strictest applicable sovereign maximum for the exact packaged-water form in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, control where no defensible sovereign number exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Pb.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for packaged drinking water (EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B end-state value; matched by FDA 21 CFR 165.110, Health Canada and NHMRC)
Pb.substantiation: Lead at 5 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum and it is corroborated four ways: the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, the FDA bottled-water allowable level at 21 CFR 165.110 (0.005 mg/L), the Health Canada maximum acceptable concentration and the NHMRC health-based guideline value. The Directive's 5 µg/L is its end-state value, which member states must meet by 12 January 2036 and below which the transitional value of 10 µg/L applies until then; HMTc adopts the end-state value now, so this cell is stricter than currently-enforced EU practice, but the FDA value of 5 µg/L is in force today and is independently sufficient to compel the number. The looser 10 µg/L values (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, the WHO provisional guideline value, and the Codex/mineral-water family) are named in the candidate set and are not selected because the method takes the strictest applicable value.

Cd.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cd.label: disclosed read-across from the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines health-based guideline value; the ADWG governs drinking-water supplies rather than packaged product, and Australia's packaged-water cadmium cell is absent from the register
Cd.substantiation: Cadmium at 2 µg/L is the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines health-based guideline value (0.002 mg/L, nhmrc2025_cd_drinking_water_2), the strictest cadmium value any government sets for water. It is published as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS and not as a direct maximum for this product form, and the reason is stated rather than left to inference. The register records that instrument's product scope as 'drinking water' and its note describes it as a health-based guideline value; the Australian Drinking Water Guidelines are a non-statutory guideline for drinking-water supplies, and Australia regulates packaged water not under the ADWG but under the FSANZ Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code. No FSANZ packaged-water metals row exists in the register: of the AU, NZ and AU-NZ rows, the only water-scoped entries are the eight NHMRC drinking-water guideline values, and Schedule 19 is represented only by commodity rows (formula, cereals, fish, salt and the like). The Australian packaged-water cadmium cell is therefore absent from the register and is logged as a register gap, in the same way Commission Directive 2003/40/EC is logged on the mineral-water row. The category's two textual packaged-water bridges do not carry this instrument either: FDA 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) incorporates the EPA maximum contaminant levels (cadmium 5 µg/L) and EU Directive 2020/2184's scope reaches water put into bottles or containers (cadmium 5 µg/L), and neither reaches an Australian guideline. Absence of a packaged-product carve-out is not affirmative scope, so the earlier regulatory-alignment tag overstated what this instrument does. WHAT THE INSTRUMENTS SET FOR THE EXACT CELL IS STATED OPENLY, because the read-across runs in the protective direction and nothing is served by concealing it: the strictest maximum level any government sets for cadmium in this exact packaged-water form is 3 µg/L, then 5 µg/L (EU Drinking Water Directive eu20202184_cd_drinking_water_5, FDA 21 CFR 165.110 fda21cfr165110_cd_bottled_water_5, EPA MCL epa2018_cd_drinking_water_5, California us_ca_swrcb_2024_cd_cadmium_mcl_5ugl), then 7 µg/L (Health Canada healthcanada2025_cd_drinking_water_7). HMTc publishes the stricter 2 µg/L: the substance and the basis are identical, HMTc does not relax a published limit toward a looser instrument, and the value is unchanged from the earlier compilation. Only the provenance tag is corrected, from regulatory-alignment to read-across, so that the record never claims a sovereign packaged-water maximum that no sovereign has written. The 3 µg/L tier for this exact form is Hong Kong Cap 132V (hk_cap132v_cd_bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters-other-than-natural_3), Israel FCS 2016 (il_fcs2016_cd_17_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_3) and Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011 (vn_qcvn8_2_2011_cd_bottled-water_3), with the WHO guideline value (who2022_cd_drinking_water_3) at the same figure.

tAs.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
tAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum; unanimous at 10 µg/L across the applicable instrument pool
tAs.substantiation: Total arsenic at 10 µg/L is unanimous across every applicable instrument in the pool: EU Drinking Water Directive, FDA 21 CFR 165.110, the EPA MCL adopted into the bottled-water standard of quality by reference, California, Health Canada, NHMRC, Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011 and the WHO provisional guideline value. There is no stricter sovereign total-arsenic value for water anywhere in the register. Total arsenic is published as its own cell and is not satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell.

iAs.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
iAs.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum for the exact product form (Israel FCS 2016 row 16.1, bottled drinking water and mineral water)
iAs.substantiation: Inorganic arsenic at 6 µg/L is the Israel FCS 2016 maximum level for the exact product form ('Bottled drinking water and mineral water', source row 16.1, 0.006 mg/kg), the strictest sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum for packaged water in the register. The alternatives are the US EPA drinking-water MCL recorded as inorganic arsenic at 10 µg/L and the Chilean Decreto 977/1996 Article 160 value of 10 µg/L for mineral and packaged drinking waters; both are named and neither is selected because 6 µg/L is applicable and stricter. The species cell is retained separately from total arsenic even though arsenic in potable water is effectively all inorganic, because the HMTc panel never allows a species to satisfy a total: a lot must clear both 10 µg/L total arsenic and 6 µg/L inorganic arsenic.

tHg.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
tHg.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B; matched by NHMRC, Health Canada and Israel FCS 2016)
tHg.substantiation: Total mercury at 1 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign maximum, set independently by the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B, the NHMRC health-based guideline, the Health Canada maximum acceptable concentration (which the source table states applies to all forms of mercury) and the Israel FCS 2016 packaged-water line. The FDA bottled-water allowable level and the California MCL are 2 µg/L and the Vietnamese bottled-water value is 6 µg/L; all are named and none is selected. Total mercury is published as a total and is never satisfied by a methylmercury or inorganic-mercury result.

MeHg.rationale: Mercury in sealed packaged drinking water is present essentially as inorganic Hg(II). Methylation is a microbial process requiring anaerobic sulfate- or iron-reducing activity in sediment or biota; it does not occur in a treated, filtered, disinfected and sealed packaged-water matrix, and there is no aquatic food chain in the product to bioaccumulate methylmercury. Methylmercury is in any event a component of total mercury, so it is bounded by identity at the published total-mercury ceiling of 1 µg/L. No separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Methylmercury is not separately quantified as a routine cell. Total mercury is measured on every certification lot by cold-vapour atomic fluorescence or ICP-MS against the published total-mercury ceiling. Where a lot result reaches or exceeds half the total-mercury ceiling, speciation by GC-ICP-MS or HPLC-ICP-MS is run as a reflex and the source water is investigated; a detectable methyl fraction is an immediate non-conformance regardless of the total-mercury result.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction in the register sets a methylmercury maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water: of the 27 methylmercury rows in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, every one is a fish or aquatic-animal tissue limit and none is water-scoped. Every drinking-water and packaged-water instrument in the pool regulates mercury as total mercury with no methyl line, and Hong Kong Cap 132V regulates the packaged-drinking-water mercury cell as INORGANIC mercury (0.006 mg/kg, hk_cap132v_ihg_bottled-or-packaged-drinking-waters-other-than-natural_6), which is direct sovereign confirmation that the regulated mercury species in packaged water is the inorganic one. The only methylmercury maxima anywhere in the register are fish and aquatic-animal limits (for example fda_cpg540600_mehg_fish_1000), which govern a bioaccumulating tissue matrix and have no application to water.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I; EU Commission Directive 2003/40/EC (natural mineral waters — ABSENT from the register and logged as a register gap; this determination does not rest on it, and it is re-tested when the instrument is ingested); US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110; California SWRCB Title 22 s.64431; Health Canada Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality (2025 summary tables); NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines; WHO Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality; Hong Kong Cap 132V Part 2; Israel FCS 2016; India FSSAI 2016; Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011; GSO 193/2021; Colombia Res 4506/2013; Chile Decreto 977/1996; Fiji FSR 2009.

Ni.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Ni.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B; matched by NHMRC)
Ni.substantiation: Nickel at 20 µg/L is the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, matched exactly by the NHMRC health-based guideline and by the Hong Kong Cap 132V natural-mineral-waters line. The looser candidates are Hong Kong's 70 µg/L for other packaged drinking waters, the WHO guideline value of 70 µg/L, and 100 µg/L from FDA 21 CFR 165.110 and California; all are named and none is selected. The FDA and California nickel values descend from an EPA nickel MCL that was remanded in 1995, which is a further reason not to treat 100 µg/L as the operative ceiling when a current statutory value of 20 µg/L is applicable.

Sn.rationale: No sovereign sets a tin maximum for drinking water, bottled water or natural mineral water. The drinking-water instrument family carries no tin parameter at all (EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I Parts B and C; US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; US FDA 21 CFR 165.110 standards of quality; Health Canada; NHMRC; WHO), and none of the national food-schedule packaged-water lines (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Israel FCS 2016, India FSSAI 2016, Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, GSO 193/2021, Colombia Res 4506/2013, Chile Decreto 977/1996, Fiji FSR 2009) carries a tin entry for water. A read-across is not supportable: the nearest sovereign tin maxima are the canned-food and canned-beverage maximum levels, which exist to bound dissolution of tin from a tinplate container wall into an acidic canned matrix, and the canned-beverage value (100 mg/kg inorganic tin) sits roughly four orders of magnitude above anything a packaged water can plausibly contain, so importing it would publish a ceiling that functions as no limit at all. The dominant packaging for this category (PET, HDPE, glass, aluminium) contains no tin. Still bottled water is occasionally presented in aluminium or tin-free steel cans, neither of which is a tin source. Tin therefore remains a mandatory control cell; no number is invented.
Sn.reference_method: Tin by ICP-MS on the finished packaged product in its native per-litre as-consumed basis, on every certification lot, reported against the method limit of quantification rather than a ceiling. Any quantifiable tin result triggers investigation of the container, closure and liner, the filling line and the source water, and lot release is withheld pending root-cause identification and a clean re-test. Where the product is presented in a tinplate or tin-coated container, the EU canned-beverage inorganic-tin maximum level recorded as the companion instrument applies as a regulatory hard stop in addition to this control.

companions.scope: canned beverages, including canned fruit and vegetable juices, except ca

Al.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Al.label: strictest applicable sovereign value; an indicator / secondary / aesthetic parameter, disclosed as such
Al.substantiation: Aluminium at 200 µg/L is the strictest applicable sovereign value and is disclosed here as a non-health-based parameter rather than a toxicological line: it is an Annex I Part C INDICATOR parameter in the EU Drinking Water Directive, a SECONDARY (aesthetically based) allowable level at FDA 21 CFR 165.110, and an AESTHETIC guideline for acid-soluble aluminium in the NHMRC guidelines. The health-based alternatives are far looser (Health Canada's maximum acceptable concentration of 2900 µg/L; California's MCL of 1000 µg/L), so adopting 200 µg/L is the strictest applicable treatment and is materially protective. Its aesthetic derivation is stated rather than concealed because the label of the parameter, not only its number, is part of the provenance.

Cr.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cr.label: strictest applicable sovereign maximum (EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B end-state value)
Cr.substantiation: Total chromium at 25 µg/L is the EU Drinking Water Directive Annex I Part B parametric value, the strictest applicable sovereign maximum; it is the Directive's end-state value, to be met by 12 January 2036, with a transitional value of 50 µg/L in force until then. The 50 µg/L tier (Hong Kong Cap 132V, Health Canada, WHO, California) and the 100 µg/L tier (EPA MCL, FDA 21 CFR 165.110) are named and not selected. This cell is published as a FIRM limit rather than as a screen, which is a deliberate departure from the HMTc default for total chromium and is compelled by the instruments themselves: in a food matrix total chromium is dominated by nutritionally benign Cr(III) and is a poor proxy for the health-relevant species, but the drinking-water instruments regulate total chromium precisely because the two species interconvert in aqueous media, and the Health Canada entry states in terms that the maximum acceptable concentration protects against chromium(VI) effects and is established for total chromium. The hexavalent species is not displaced: it is published separately at 10 µg/L.

Cr-VI.basis: µg/L of finished packaged water, as consumed (numerically equal to µg/kg at unit density)
Cr-VI.label: disclosed read-across from the California SWRCB Title 22 s.64431 hexavalent-chromium maximum contaminant level for public water systems; no government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for any packaged-water form
Cr-VI.substantiation: The exact cell is unregulated, and the record says so on its face rather than asserting a maximum no government has written for this product form. No jurisdiction in the register sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum for bottled water, packaged water or natural mineral water, and neither of the two textual packaged-water bridges this category relies on reaches the species: FDA 21 CFR 165.110(b)(4)(iii) incorporates the EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulation maximum contaminant levels and EPA sets no hexavalent-chromium MCL, and EU Directive 2020/2184 Annex I carries no hexavalent-chromium parameter. The nearest applicable sovereign value is therefore the California State Water Resources Control Board Title 22 section 64431 Table 64431-A maximum contaminant level of 10 µg/L (0.01 mg/L, us_ca_swrcb_2024_cr-vi_chromium-hexavalent_mcl_10ugl), re-adopted in 2024 after health-risk and feasibility analysis, and it is carried across as a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS. Two hops are disclosed rather than argued around. First, SCOPE: the register records that instrument's product scope as 'public water systems in California', which is utility-delivered tap water and not a packaged good; HMTc has not identified, and does not cite, any California provision applying Title 22 section 64431 maximum contaminant levels to bottled water sold in the state, so this cell must not be read as an assertion that California enforces 10 µg/L against a packaged product. Second, SOVEREIGNTY: California is a sub-national government. The only alternative anywhere in the register is the NHMRC Australian Drinking Water Guidelines statement that hexavalent chromium should not exceed 50 µg/L (nhmrc2025_crvi_drinking_water_50), which is five times looser and carries the same drinking-water scope hop; it is named here and not selected because the method takes the strictest applicable value. The value is unchanged from the earlier compilation at 10 µg/L; only the provenance tag is corrected, from regulatory-alignment to read-across. HMTc publishes Cr-VI as its own cell in addition to total chromium: a hexavalent result never satisfies the total-chromium cell and a total-chromium result never satisfies this one, and the total-chromium cell on this row is a direct sovereign maximum for the product form that bounds this species from above.
